instance: Team Lead broadcast HALT to all 14 commanders during Operation Multi-Variant Deployment; after resolving the blocker, aggressive commanders (Patton, Halsey) inferred resumption from context and continued, but methodical commanders (Spruance, Bradley) waited for an explicit RESUME order — Spruance sat idle for 10 hours before the Team Lead discovered he was still halted.
check: After any HALT, send an explicit RESUME broadcast to ALL commanders as soon as the blocker is resolved, and periodically confirm every halted commander has actually resumed rather than assuming inference.

instance: Across 14 deployed website variants, TypeScript strict-mode compilation passed at only a 93% rate (not 100%), and this sub-100% result was accepted as within an unstated acceptable threshold rather than requiring fixes before deployment.

Functional testing covered only 5 of 14 deployed variants (36% sample) rather than all variants, and the 50/50 pass rate on that partial sample was treated as sufficient confidence for the full 14-variant campaign.
Brand/voice consistency review sampled only 6 of 14 deployed variants (43%) for biographical accuracy and brand standards rather than reviewing every deliverable before sign-off.

source_anchor: Commander Behavior Observations > Aggressive Commanders (Patton, Halsey, MacArthur)
instance: Aggressive-personality commanders were observed to rush or skip validation steps for speed, overlook edge cases, and add unrequested features (scope creep) when deployed without explicit guardrails.

source_anchor: Commander Behavior Observations > Methodical Commanders (Spruance, Bradley, Nimitz)
instance: Methodical-personality commanders halt and wait indefinitely rather than proceed when uncertain, requiring explicit reassurance/authorization to continue — the behavioral root cause of the Spruance 10-hour stall described in the HALT/RESUME incident.
check: Apply explicit RESUME discipline for this commander class rather than assuming they will infer authorization.

source_anchor: Timeline Estimation Lessons > Personality-Based Duration Multipliers
instance: Baseline timeline estimates (2-3 hours per variant) did not account for commander personality: aggressive commander Patton finished in ~0.5x-0.7x baseline while methodical commander Spruance took 1.3x-1.5x baseline, so a single flat estimate was inaccurate at both ends of the roster.
check: Apply a personality-based duration multiplier to baseline task estimates instead of one flat figure per task type.

source_anchor: Timeline Estimation Lessons > Parallel Execution Scaling
instance: Running 14 fronts in parallel completed in ~18 hours versus an estimated 35 hours if run sequentially (14 x 2.5h) — only ~50% scaling efficiency rather than a full 14x speedup — indicating coordination overhead was not fully modeled in the parallel-execution estimate.

source_anchor: Error Handling Lessons > Commander Not Responding
instance: When Spruance stopped responding for 10 hours, the team's first instinct was to treat it as an unresponsive-commander problem rather than immediately checking whether an explicit RESUME order had actually been sent after the prior HALT.
check: Before escalating a non-responding commander, first verify whether a RESUME broadcast was actually sent after the last HALT.

source_anchor: Error Handling Lessons > Quality Gate Failures
instance: No quality gate failures occurred in Operation Multi-Variant Deployment (100% pass rate across all 3 gates); the document attributes this to pre-deployment personality-to-task matching rather than to any corrective control that actually caught a failure in flight.
